He remains chief executive, leading a global payments business built around proprietary transaction technology.

long_biography.plain_text:
Smith founded InComm in an Atlanta garage in 1992 to support prepaid long-distance phone cards. The decisive advance was point-of-sale activation: instead of stocking cards with preloaded value, retailers could activate products at checkout. InComm refined that model and extended it into wireless, gift cards, digital content and other payment products.

He remained chief executive as the company expanded internationally and added businesses through acquisitions. A Warburg Pincus fund made a minority investment in 2012; it was an investment in InComm, not a measure of Smith's personal wealth. He is also a director and controlling shareholder of InComm Europe. His exact current interest in every global InComm entity is not publicly disclosed, so corporate revenue, transaction volume and other company assets are not treated as his personal fortune.
